newsitem.title: INDIA: Calcutta shares slump on U.S. action in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Calcutta shares slump on U.S. action in Iraq.

text.p: Share prices slumped after a strong opening and closed lower on the Calcutta bourse in reaction to reports of U.S. bombing of Iraq, brokers said.

They said that prices were firm on opening but fresh selling surfaced during early trades on reports that the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) would be taking punitive action against brokers for doing illegal carryforward trading.
While this dampened buying sentiments, prices of blue-chips plunged further as soon as fresh reports came in that U.S. planes had bombed Iraq, brokers said.
"The news from Iraq has come at the worst possible time," said a dealer at Ratnabali Securities.
"Till yesterday there had been signs of Indian stocks getting into the recovery mode," he said. "Some amount of investment buying of medium-cap stocks also was evident."
"But now the recovery has been nipped and blue-chips are unlikely to gain enough momentum to breach the upside resistance," the dealer added.
